wiki.title: Tower of Vane
wiki.description: The Tower of Vane is a spectacular sight, rising from the Grey Mountains far above Ubersreik; it can be seen for many miles around. It appears almost as a needle, tall and virtually featureless, formed from the stark rocky landscape, and crowned by a glass dome. The place is a centre of Celestial divination away from the confusing signs of Altdorf, a lofty peak where the Celestial Wizards can survey the portents in splendid isolation, surrounded in the dominant wind of Azyr.

wiki.description: The Lorlay is a jagged, rocky island situated in the River Reik, about 40 miles downstream from Grissenwald. wiki.description: Glimdwarrow is the largest Gnomic community in the Empire of Man, located south of Middenland. Glimdwarrow is to be found beneath the hill range known as the Mirror Moors and numbers nearly a thousand inhabitants.

wiki.title: Drakwald College of the Holy Wolf
wiki.description: Poking through the shadowy canopy of the Drakwald Forest, far from the Middenheim to Altdorf road, is a steep rocky outcrop, topped with a lonely-looking Ulrican temple. This is a temple that serves no village, a temple with no worshippers or congregations, yet it is one of the cult's most important temples. This temple is the Drakwald College of the Holy Wolf, a renowned Ulrican seminary, famous for the devotion and piety of the priests it produces, and infamous for the brutal regime to which its initiates are subjected.

wiki.title: Temple of the Red Coral
wiki.description: The Temple of the Red Coral is a small but well-tended temple that sits on the coastline just north of the town of Salzenmund. It is so named for the mysterious red coral that grows in the area, unusual in the chill waters of the northern sea, and pieces of which were used in the building's construction. The cult sees the coral, as well as the large numbers of fish that congregate there, as a sign of Manann's blessing.

wiki.title: Helspire
wiki.description: Helspire is a haunted fortress carved out of the rock of the the Grey Mountains near Axe Bite Pass. Typically, Helspire appears to be long abandoned. However, on some nights, eerie lights shine from the castle.

properties.name: Blackstone Tower
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Core Rulebook

wiki.title: Blackstone Tower
wiki.description: Blackstone Tower is an Imperial -built fortress under the dominion of the Dwarf kingdom of Karak Ziflin that guards the pass known as the Crooked Corridor in the Grey Mountains. The Crooked Corridor was an obscure passage over the Grey Mountains until several decades ago, when a series of Goblin invasions crossed into Reikland by the route. In response, Emperor Mattheus II commissioned the construction of a fortress to guard the pass.

properties.name: Castle Drachenfels
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Core Rulebook

wiki.title: Castle Drachenfels
wiki.description: Castle Drachenfels is the ancient home of the foul necromancer Constant Drachenfels, located in the Grey Mountains between the territories of Bretonnia and the Empire.. Like the twisted talon of a malformed claw, the seven towers of Castle Drachenfels clutch at the sky in a gesture of malevolence and spite. Each of its misshapen turrets is festooned with windows, resembling eyes without number, alert to the arrival of any traveller unlucky --or unwise -- enough to stumble upon the lair of the Great Enchanter.

wiki.title: Castle Drakenhof
wiki.description: Castle Drakenhof was the former capital of the Imperial province of Sylvania during the reign of its last Imperial noble, Count Otto von Drak. Nearly all the rulers of Sylvania, living and Undead alike, have made the castle their seat of power.

wiki.title: Fort Denkh
wiki.description: Over 1,000 years old, Fort Denkh stands on the border between Middenland and Hochland. Constructed during the tumultuous Age of Three Emperors, it was used to protect Middenland from Hochland troops trying to pass undetected through the Drakwald. Ever since, this old fortress has changed hands many times as the land on which it sits has changed hands between the Counts.

wiki.title: Castle Lenkster
wiki.description: Castle Lenkster is an Empire fort in Ostland, which overlooks a border crossing that leads through the Middle Mountains to Hochland. Originally it housed around 200 inhabitants, but it was sacked in 2522 IC and today there are only 20 people left, most of them border guards under Elector Count Valmir von Raukov 's pay. It is said that the mountains where it stands were once cursed by the last Dwarf priests of Karaz Ghumzul.

When Vlad von Carstein was defeated at the Siege of Altdorf in 2051 IC, the Elector Count of Stirland ordered the building of a castle to monitor and safeguard the western roads that lead into Sylvania. It took twenty-three years to build Fort Oberstyre, but it was worth it, for the castle became the very pinnacle of military architecture in the impoverished region it occupies.

names.fr: Le Donjon De La Corne De Taal

wiki.title: Taal's Horn Keep
wiki.description: Taal's Horn Keep is an ancient, semi-ruined fortress located in the Grey Mountains. It serves as the home of the Ubersreik Five, as well as their two allies, Franz Lohner and Olesya Pimenova.

properties.name: Tancred Castle
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

properties.name: Grasgar Castle
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Grasgar Castle
wiki.description: Grasgar Castle is the current home of Duke Taubert and the newest large castle in Bretonnia.

properties.name: Castle Rachard

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Barony of the Damned

properties.name: Turris Vigilans
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Turris Vigilans
wiki.description: Turris Vigilans is a temple of Verena that stands on an isolated headland in the north of Bordeleaux. It serves as a lighthouse and has a reputation of one of the most reliable in the world. Its primary purpose, however, is to keep a watch on Mousillon.

properties.name: Castle Desfleuve
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Castle Desfleuve
wiki.description: Castle Desfleuve stands at the centre of the Gisoreux Gap. It is the seat of the Marquis Desfleuve, a young man charged with coordinating the defence of the whole pass. He is the only child of his parents: his mother died in childbirth and his father died less than a year ago.

properties.name: Sanglac Castle
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Sanglac Castle
wiki.description: Sanglac Castle is an abandoned castle in the heart of the Grey Mountains. A century ago, messengers found it full of the corpses of the noble family living there, mixed with the Orcs they had slain. This is not too unusual, so another noble family was allowed to send a younger son to take over.

properties.name: Castle Gransette
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

properties.name: Château d'Epee
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

properties.name: Castle Garamont
properties.source: Knight Errant (Novel) by Anthony Reynolds

wiki.title: Castle Garamont
wiki.description: Castle Garamont is the ancient seat of power for the Castellan of Bastonne and thus the first line of defence for the entire dukedom. It was also the birthplace and home of the famed Grail Knight Calard, the Grail Damsel Anara and the fallen Blood Knight, Bertelis.

properties.name: Castle Sangasse
properties.source: Warhammer: Knights of Bretonnia (Omnibus)

wiki.title: Castle Sangasse
wiki.description: Castle Sangasse was a great Bretonnian Castle situated in the dukedom of Bastonne, where it served as the seat of power for Maloric, the Earl of Sangasse.

properties.name: Castle Artois
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Castle Artois
wiki.description: Castle Artois is a Fortress-City and the ducal capital of Artois, located on the borders of the Forest of Arden. During the reign of Louen Orc-Slayer Artois was the home of Duchess Artemis and ringed by a large stone wall and stake-filled ditches to protect it from roving warbands of vile Beastmen.

properties.name: Barley Motte
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Barley Motte
wiki.description: Barley Motte is in the north of Lyonesse, close to the border with L'Anguille. Two centuries ago it was the home of the D'ayvle lords, who cooperated with the Ruinous Powers and plotted to bring down the nation. They were defeated by a group of bold adventurers, one of whom was rewarded with the fief.

properties.name: Castle Aquin
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Battles (5th Edition): Circle of Blood

properties.name: Summersfall Fort
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Summersfall Fort
wiki.description: Summersfall Fort is a medium-size hill fort in east of Carcassonne. It is famous for being definitely haunted. If a small group of people spends the night of the last day of summer within the walls of the fort, they encounter the Ghost of the Glanborien noble who once lived here.

properties.name: Garban Hold
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Garban Hold
wiki.description: Garban Hold is an Orc warren, and the Duke of Montfort would love to know exactly where it is. Captured Orcs and Goblins have mentioned it under torture, and recent raids do seem to have been more coordinated. It is probably somewhere in the centre of Montfort, and there is likely to be an Orc Warboss in control.

properties.name: Gaudaron Keep
properties.source: White Dwarf 310

wiki.title: Amalric of Gaudaron
wiki.description: Sir Amalric of Gaudaron, also known as the Bane of the Undead, was a famed Grail Knight of Bretonnia.

properties.name: Crac de Sang
properties.source: The Red Duke (Novel) by C. L. Werner

wiki.title: Crac de Sang
wiki.description: The fortress Crac de Sang was the seat of the Bretonnian Vampire Lord known as the Red Duke, constructed by hundreds of enslaved Aquitanians whom the Vampire forced to build his new fortress for having stood aside as his wife was lost to despair over his apparent death and usurpers had plotted to take control of his dukedom of Aquitaine. Constructed upon a hill overlooking the River Morceaux and the Forest of Chalons, the fortress was located at a strategically vital angle, allowing watch posts to see as far as the Massif Orcal. The old dukes of Aquitaine had commissioned a watchtower to be constructed upon it, but it fell into disrepair and was abandoned long before the Red Duke came to claim the site as his own.

properties.name: Château Lovarre
properties.source: Warhammer Monthly 27

wiki.title: Château Lovarre
wiki.description: Château Lovarre is a Bretonnian castle located in Carcassonne in southern Bretonnia, near the Tilean border. Given the position of the castle on the borderlands between the two realms, Lovarre is a prime target for annexation by the Tileans. Despite this, the settlement is far from the thoroughfares of Bretonnia, and its defence is left to the soldiers of Lord Tibault, the ruler of the castle.

properties.name: Château de Chegney
properties.source: Brunner the Bounty Hunter Omnibus (Novel) by C.L. Werner

wiki.title: Chateau de Chegney
wiki.description: The Chateau de Chegney is a castle ruled by the Viscount Augustine de Chegney. The centuries hung heavy within the great hall of the Chateau de Chegney. For a thousand years House de Chegney had dwelled in the massive, brooding, stone fortress, guarding the narrow Iron Pass through the Grey Mountains that linked the Kingdom of Bretonnia with the sprawling Empire.

properties.name: Donjon de Dol
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Barony of the Damned

properties.name: Fort Bergbres
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 1e: Marienburg - Sold Down the River

wiki.title: Fort Bergbres
wiki.description: In the middle of the Ois Gap at the bridge over the River Ois squats Fort Bergbres, a former Imperial castle now run jointly by the Marienburg Directorate and agents appointed by the Duke of Gisoreux of Bretonnia. It has a population of 225 and serves as a rest station and supply post for those preparing for the long trek across the Bitter Moors or refitting after crossing it. There is a large joint force of excisemen and roadwardens stationed here to guard against smugglers and protect travellers against the dangers waiting in the hills.

properties.name: Castle Alexandronov
properties.source: Citadel Journal #14

wiki.title: Castle Alexandronov
wiki.description: Castle Alexandronov stands to the North of Erengrad, on the borders of the Troll country. Construction of the castle was originally ordered by the great Tzar Alexandr Njevski. He chose the site guided by a dream in which Boris Ursa, the Forever Tzar of Kislev, directed him to build a great stronghold for Kislev, or else the land would be lost in a war against the greatest evil of all.

wiki.title: Castello di Rugazzi
wiki.description: Castello di Rugazzi is a Tilean castle famous for its vineyards. The place was burned down when the rest of Tilea was destroyed during the End Times. The Goblin chieftain Skarsnik quite probably drank from the last bottle of wine ever created from the castle's vineyard, if not the last bottle ever made in Tilea, but not before checking if it was poisoned by letting one of his Snotlings taste it.

properties.source: Warhammer: The Old World

wiki.title: Louen Keep
wiki.description: Louen Keep is an ancient and near-impregnable fort in the Border Princes that has long been held by a succession of Bretonnian exiles, all tasked with defending the south-eastern approaches to their homeland. Circa 2276 IC, Loeun Keep had become the stronghold of Sir Cecil Gastonne, a renowed Bretonnian exile known as the Wyrm Slayer.

properties.source: Warhammer: The Old World

wiki.title: Dragon Falls
wiki.description: Situated beyond the recognised borders of Bretonnia, where The Vaults meet the Irrana Mountains, Dragon Falls is an impregnable fortress, manned year-round by knights of Carcassonne. The fortress shares its name with a waterfall on the upper reaches of the River Songez that probably got its name from the rock formations and mist, which make it look rather like a dragon breathing smoke. Some people believe a Dragon once lived here, and that its treasure remains.

properties.name: The Picket
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: The Horned Rat

wiki.title: The Picket
wiki.description: The Picket is a fortification built on the orders of Emperor Magnus the Pious to keep the Brass Keep and its Nurglish denizens contained within the Middle Mountains of the northern Empire. The Picket consists of a ring-wall surrounding the keep and its hinterland, strengthened with wall-forts and supplied by two great depots in Middenland and Ostland. It is manned by the personal troops of House Kärzburdger.

wiki.description: Fortress of the Sun is an Estalian sea-fortress of the realm of Cantonia which faces the eastern shores of the Bay of Quietude, mirroring Magritta 's Fortress of the Moon.

wiki.title: Fortress of the Moon
wiki.description: The Fortress of the Moon is a fortress of the Estalian Kingdom of Magritta which faces the eastern shores of the Bay of Quietude, mirroring the neighbouring kingdom of Cantonia 's Fortress of the Sun.

This suspicion is due to the fact that cloaked agents and ornate coaches have converged upon Castle Sternieste with increasing frequency and that von Korden himself has witnessed a pale lord on its walls.

The mercenary band known as the Birdmen of Catrazza were commissioned by a trader to steal it from the dreaded tower.

wiki.description: Fort Solace is a small seaside village built around a lighthouse along the northern shore of the Manaanspoort Sea. It is a new settlement, founded after the destruction of Almshoven and its beacon on the opposite shore during the last incursion of the forces of Chaos into the Wasteland. Fort Solace is owned outright by the Wasteland Import-Export Exchange of Marienburg, and its governor is a 'Change employee.

wiki.title: Brandy Home
wiki.description: Brandy Home is a fortified structure of stone located near the summit of the Brenheim Pass in the Vaults, between Tilea and the Empire. Built centuries ago and held by the same Human family since, it is here that, between the spring melt and the autumn frosts, Dwarfs from The Vaults and the western Black Mountains come to trade with Imperials and Tileans, and to sample the inn's famous brandy.

properties.name: Zanbaijin
properties.source: Total War: Warhammer III

wiki.title: Zanbaijin
wiki.description: Zanbaijin, called the " Fallen City," was a ruined city older than Mankind, and had long served as an arena where the Chaos Gods watched their mortal followers vie for their favour in violent conflict. Located on the blasted plateau of K'datha in the Eastern Steppes, when the Chaos Champions and their armies came to battle here, each one hoped to prove their worth and the superiority of their patron deity over all others. A Chaos Champion who was a victor here would be marked for greatness, and by ancient tradition become master of those they vanquished.

wiki.title: Altar of the Crimson Harvest
wiki.description: The Altar of the Crimson Harvest is a Sarl tribal fortress and port town located in the Troll Country of Norsca that is shared with the Skaelings, to both tribes' benefit. It is a port trading mainly in the living victims of Skaeling slave raids: the so-called "Crimson Harvest." Captives from many tribes, nations, and species are brought here and introduced to their new life as thralls to the Norscans. Besides maritime traffic there are regular caravans taking thralls and other items through the safer passes to Norscan settlements deeper in the mountains.

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 4e: Enemy in Shadows

wiki.title: Darkstone Ring
wiki.description: The Darkstone Ring is a malign monument in Reikland, north of Blutroch near the Altdorf - Bögenhafen road. It consists of six suggestively-carved standing stones arranged in a ring, and a sacrificial slab of unidentifiable rock in the center. At night, the ring's six stones glow green.

wiki.title: The Singing Stones
wiki.description: The Singing Stones are an ancient megalithic monument in Reikland, located in a wooded valley west of Schädelheim. The monument is centered around a central dolmen- a flat slab placed on top of several pillar-like stones, resembling a huge altar. From this dolmen, rows of menhirs spiral out.

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Guerac Circle
wiki.description: Mousillon was not always a cursed land, though the blight does date back centuries. Guerac Circle is one of the few places remaining from before the horror. A stone circle sacred to Taal and Rhya, it stands in the hills of northern Mousillon, surrounded by an area of healthy vegetation and wholesome wildlife.

properties.name: Barrows of Cuileux
properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Knights of the Grail

wiki.title: Barrows of Cuileux
wiki.description: The Barrows of Cuileux should not be confused with the Grave of Cuileux. The Grave is the site of the last battle between the Knights of Cuileux and the Greenskin horde. The Barrows of Cuileux are where the Cuilen buried their dead.

properties.source: Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay 2e: Barony of the Damned

wiki.title: Farulin's Brothers
wiki.description: In the north-east of Mousillon, just south of the Forest of Arden, stand scores of monoliths in complex arrangements of concentric circles. No one knows who Farulin actually was or what the stones signify, but peasants who go missing in the area can often be found sitting by one of the monoliths, staring up at the sky. They cannot be woken from this dull state of awareness for several days.
